summary: Thomas Bond Lindsay was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Genesee Wesleyan Seminary, Boston Latin School, Wesleyan University (M.A.), and Boston University (Ph.D.). He taught at Newton High School (1877–1888) and Boston University as Assistant Professor of Latin and Sanskrit (1878–1909).

Thomas Borchert works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago under scholars including Bruce Lincoln, Martin Riesebrodt, and Donald K. Swearer. He is attested in 2017 as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont.

Thomas Bruce Ridgeway worked in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington by 1986 and served there as Director of the Center for Computing and Humanities from circa 1986 to 1994.

Thomas Burrow was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge under E. J. Rapson and at SOAS and Annamalai. He held posts at the British Museum, SOAS, and Oxford, serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit and fellow of Balliol (1944–1976).

Thomas Callan Hodson worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at The Queen's College, Oxford. He served as Registrar at Queen Mary University of London (1903–1914), Principal of Thornsey Training College (1921–1923), and Reader of Ethnography at Cambridge (1926–1937).

Thomas Candy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Magdalen College School. He served at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as Superintendent in 1837 and later as Principal from 1851 to 1857.

Thomas Chalmers was a scholar of religion who studied at the University of St Andrews and the University of Edinburgh. He later held academic posts at the University of St Andrews (circa 1823–1828) and the University of Edinburgh (circa 1828–1843).

Thomas Christian Tychsen was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Kiel and Göttingen, learning under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He spent his career at Göttingen, appointed ao. Professor of Theology in 1785 and ord. Professor of Philosophy in 1788.

Thomas Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, completed a Ph.D. at Harvard University, and earned a JD at the University of California, Berkeley.
Thomas Craven was a scholar in the fields of linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.D. from Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary and an M.A. from Northwestern University.

Thomas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans and Christian K. Wedemeyer, as well as several traditional Tibetan teachers, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow is an art historian who studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Princeton, Chicago, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, directed the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor at NYU in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indologist and historian who studied at Eton, East India Company College, and under Jagannatha. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Erskine Perry was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Charterhouse School, Trinity College, Cambridge, and the University of Munich. He served as a Judge of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Bombay (1841–1852) and member of the Council of India (1859–1882).
Thomas Ethelbert Page was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Shrewsbury School and St John's College. He held a long-standing post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University, earning his PhD under Robert A. F. Thurman in 2003. He was attested as Executive Editor at Columbia University in 2007.

Thomas Fulton Cummings was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Union Theological Seminary, Pittsburgh Theological Seminary, and Westminster College. He taught at Jhelum Theological Seminary, Biblical Seminary in New York, Union Theological Seminary, and Drew University (1918–1933).

Thomas George Percival Spear was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He taught history at St. Stephen's College, Delhi (1924–1940) and held posts at Selwyn College and the University of Cambridge.

Thomas Grahame Bailey was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed a D.Litt. at the University of Edinburgh by 1920. He served as Reader in Hindustani at SOAS University of London from circa 1920 to 1940.

Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, University College London, Charing Cross Hospital, and Imperial College School of Medicine. He held a post at Imperial College London from circa 1854 to 1885.
